answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: Within 15 minutes. The operator must contact MSHA immediately, and within 15 minutes, at 1-800-746-1553 once the operator knows or should know that an accident involving a death has occurred.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number once it knows or should know of an accident.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is one of the covered accidents.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent. The 0.4 percent increase per 0.1 percent of methane applies only where methane is present.

claims.text: The combined dust must keep an incombustible content of not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The percentage is increased only where methane is present in a ventilating current.
claims.quote: Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The self-rescue device must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each operator must make available to each miner going underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground metal and nonmetal mines (30 CFR 57.4361) must hold mine evacuation drills at least once every six months. The drills must be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground.

claims.text: Mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

claims.text: The drills must be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground.
claims.quote: Be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground;

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Each new miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties, with the training duplicating underground conditions as closely as practicable.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA (an 8-hour time-weighted average), or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.

claims.text: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway. This appears in both 30 CFR 56.9300 (surface metal and nonmetal mines) and 57.9300 (underground metal and nonmetal mines).

claims.text: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway (30 CFR 56.9300).
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: The same height requirement appears in 30 CFR 57.9300.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.

claims.text: Within the refuge alternative, the breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.

answers.question: What must a written bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan contain under OSHA?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not address OSHA's bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan. They cover only MSHA respiratory protection and respirable dust control plan rules.

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say at what depth OSHA requires a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box. They cover MSHA mining rules (slopes and shafts, shaft-sinking buckets, definitions, ventilation controls), not OSHA trench excavation requirements.

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The chunks do not say what FAA certification a pilot needs to fly a drone over a mine site. They cover MSHA training and certification rules, and they don't mention drones or the FAA.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The chunks do not say when a mine needs an EPA stormwater discharge permit. They cover impoundment design plans and permits for mining under water, and none of them mention EPA stormwater permits.
